title: Make identity, lease, renewal, and workload lifetimes agree
description: Choose an authenticated identity, secret contract, and client lifecycle. Then adjust TTLs and renewal timing to expose availability gaps and the credential exposure that remains after a client loses control.

identities.label: Kubernetes workload
identities.detail: A pod authenticates with its projected service-account identity and receives a renewable service token under a bounded role.

identities.label: Human OIDC session
identities.detail: A person authenticates through an identity provider; the role keeps interactive access short and reviewable.

identities.label: CI batch token
identities.detail: An ephemeral pipeline uses a non-renewable token and must finish or re-authenticate within the initial TTL.

secrets.label: Dynamic database credential
secrets.detail: Vault creates a unique external database identity and tracks it through a renewable lease.

secrets.label: Short-lived certificate
secrets.detail: A PKI role issues an identity certificate whose validity must cover connection and rotation behavior.

secrets.label: KV v2 application secret
secrets.detail: Vault versions stored data, but the external system does not automatically invalidate a copied value when the read response expires.

clientModes.label: Fetch once, no renewal
clientModes.detail: The client reads a token-backed secret at startup and has no renewal or explicit shutdown revocation path.

clientModes.label: Managed renewal
clientModes.detail: Vault Agent or equivalent client renews before expiry and reacquires material according to the role and engine contract.

clientModes.label: Bounded job with explicit revoke
clientModes.detail: A short job requests only the lifetime it needs and revokes its token tree when work completes.
